disclaimer: Not legal advice. Verify with the authority having jurisdiction before relying on a schedule.

nfpa96.title: Kitchen exhaust cleaning frequency (NFPA 96, widely republished by fire departments)
nfpa96.note: AHJs and insurers may require more frequent cleaning. Keep contractor certificates on site.

cities.name: Houston, TX
cities.agency: Houston Health Department — Special Waste / FOG Program

sources.label: Houston Health Department FOG / special waste

pumping.accumulationRule: Pump sooner if floating grease + solids reach 25% of wetted height, or if effluent limits are exceeded.
pumping.waiver: A 180-day waiver may be available after 12 months of 90-day history and demonstrated <25% accumulation.
pumping.hauler: City-permitted transporter only. Generator signs the manifest and keeps copies on site.
pumping.permit: Annual FOG / special waste generator permit; keep on site.

cities.fines: Citations commonly described in the $250–$2,000 per offense range — confirm current amounts with the city.

cities.name: Austin, TX

pumping.accumulationRule: Clean more often if grease and solids are 50% or more of wetted height (bottom of trap to invert of outlet).
pumping.waiver: Applications exist to reduce frequency below 90 days if compliance criteria are met.
pumping.hauler: City of Austin-permitted liquid waste hauler only.
pumping.permit: Follow Austin Water FOG / trap registration rules for your site.

cities.fines: Fines and permit action are possible. Confirm current penalties with Austin Water / 311.

cities.name: Dallas, TX
cities.agency: Dallas Water Utilities — Liquid Waste / Pretreatment

pumping.accumulationRule: As often as necessary but not less than every 90 days, or whenever 25% or more of the interceptor contains floating materials, sediment, oils, or grease (Dallas City Code Chapter 19, Sec. 19-126.2(c); pretreatment FAQ). Completely emptied and cleaned by a licensed hauler.
pumping.hauler: Liquid waste hauler licensed by the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality and Dallas Water Utilities. Keep manifests on site.
pumping.permit: Liquid waste generator requirements per Chapter 19 — confirm your permit status.

cities.fines: Inspectors issue citations for missed pumping, bad manifests, or over-25% accumulation. Confirm current fine schedule.

cities.name: Fort Worth, TX
cities.agency: City of Fort Worth Water — Pretreatment / Grease Traps

sources.label: Fort Worth City Code Chapter 12.5 Article VII (amlegal)

pumping.accumulationRule: Completely empty at least once every ninety (90) days, or more often if required to protect the wastewater system. The city grease-trap program page does not state a 25% accumulation trigger.
pumping.hauler: City-authorized liquid waste transporters only; use city trip tickets.
pumping.permit: Food establishments need a restaurant wastewater discharge permit before discharging to the sanitary sewer (Chapter 12.5 Article VII / §12.5-731).

cities.fines: The city grease-trap page describes penalties of up to $2,000 per violation per day. Confirm current amounts with Pretreatment.

cities.name: Chicago, IL
cities.agency: Chicago Department of Water Management / Plumbing Code; CDPH food inspections

pumping.accumulationRule: Chicago plumbing code requires interceptors to be maintained 'as often as necessary' — not a fixed 90-day clock. Keep written maintenance records for the life of the unit or at least 5 years, whichever is longer.
pumping.hauler: Use a licensed waste hauler and keep manifests.
pumping.permit: Food establishments are inspected by CDPH. Interceptor rules sit in the plumbing / water code.

cities.fines: Food inspection failures (pests, grease, sanitation) are public. Plumbing/FOG citations are separate. Confirm current penalties.

cities.name: New York City, NY
cities.agency: NYC Department of Environmental Protection — FOG / 15 RCNY §19-11

sources.label: NYC DEP disposing of grease as a business
NYC DOHMH restaurant inspections open data

pumping.accumulationRule: No fixed calendar interval. DEP: clean as frequently as necessary to avoid exceeding rated capacity. 15 RCNY §19-11(q): maintain in good working order with routine FOG and solids removal; the minimum cleaning frequency is such that accumulated fat, oil, grease, and solids do not exceed 25% of the total liquid depth the unit was designed to hold. Emulsifiers, enzymes, chemicals, and microbial additives are prohibited (§19-11(u)).
pumping.waiver: NYS PE or RA may petition the Commissioner for an equivalent alternative pretreatment device (§19-11(r)); it cannot be less stringent.
pumping.hauler: Scoop accumulated grease for recycling by a fat renderer / BIC Trade Waste Approved Company. Yellow grease (waste cooking oil) must be collected by a BIC-licensed carter; written proof of each pickup must be kept on site at least one year (§19-11(v)).
pumping.permit: Interceptors / automatic grease removal devices must be installed by an NYC Licensed Master Plumber. Commercial food waste disposers are not allowed in NYC. Units must stay accessible for DEP inspection.

cities.fines: DEP states the maximum penalty for not complying is currently $10,000 per day, per violation. Confirm current amounts with DEP.

cities.name: Phoenix, AZ
cities.agency: City of Phoenix Water Services — Environmental Services Division (FOG)

sources.label: Phoenix FOG BMP Manual for food service establishments (June 2024 PDF)

pumping.accumulationRule: Most interceptors stop working effectively when FOG and solids reach 25% of capacity; if greater than 25%, a full cleaning is required. Hydromechanical (indoor traps, typically ≤4 fixtures): fully pump every 30 days; no hydromechanical unit may go more than 90 days without maintenance unless the Director grants a variance. Gravity interceptors at food service establishments that capture FOG: fully pump at least once every 3 months unless a Director variance. New facilities should monitor accumulation and pump sooner if needed. Full pump-out by a licensed pumper; interceptor left empty; no reintroduction of water; enzymes/emulsifiers prohibited.
pumping.waiver: Director may grant a variance from the calendar frequency. Hydromechanical units still may not exceed 90 days without maintenance.
pumping.hauler: Licensed pumper. FOG mat, liquids, sludge, and scrapings go to a licensed waste disposal facility.
pumping.permit: All Phoenix FSEs that prepare food must have a grease interceptor. Hydro for up to four fixtures without a disposer or dishwasher; gravity required if a disposer, dishwasher, or more than four fixtures. Interceptor installs go through Planning and Development plan review.

cities.fines: Inspectors can require clean/replace/repair with a deadline. Confirm current penalty amounts with Phoenix Environmental Services. City Code Chapter 28 is the underlying ordinance (cited in the June 2024 BMP).

cities.name: Los Angeles, CA
cities.agency: LASAN FOG Control / LA County Public Works Industrial Waste (unincorporated)

pumping.accumulationRule: 25% rule: pump before floating FOG + settled solids reach 25% of liquid depth. High-volume fry programs often need 14–30 days in practice. City of LA FSEs typically need an industrial wastewater permit.
pumping.waiver: Alternative grease-recovery devices may be allowed with agency approval if a gravity interceptor cannot be installed.
pumping.permit: City of LA: LASAN industrial wastewater permit. Unincorporated county: IWDP via Public Works.

cities.fines: City sources cite FOG fines that can reach $1,000–$10,000/day. Confirm current schedule with LASAN or County Public Works.

cities.name: San Antonio, TX
cities.agency: San Antonio Water System (SAWS) — FOG Abatement Program

sources.label: SAWS Fats, Oils & Grease Abatement Program

pumping.accumulationRule: Sec. 34-527(b): evacuate not less often than every ninety (90) days and within two (2) working days whenever twenty-five (25) percent or more of the wetted height of the interceptor, measured from the bottom of the device to the invert of the outlet pipe, contains floating materials, sediment, fats, oils, or grease. Completely empty the unit. The Grease Procedure Manual restates 90 days or 25% of wetted depth.
pumping.waiver: FSEs/FPEs operating fewer than 120 days in a calendar year may request written SAWS approval for a calendar frequency less often than 90 days. The 25% / two-working-day trigger still applies (Sec. 34-527(b)(i)).
pumping.hauler: Interceptors greater than 100 gallons: SAWS-permitted liquid waste hauler; complete evacuation; dispose only at a permitted facility. Interceptors 100 gallons or less: permitted hauler optional; if self-evacuated, keep a cleaning log (location, type, date/time, quantity, disposal location, employee signature) (Sec. 34-527(c), 34-528).
pumping.permit: Every FSE/FPE must discharge FOG-bearing fixtures through a code-compliant interceptor (Sec. 34-526). Annual inspection by a licensed plumber or SAWS-approved professional after evacuation, with photos; defects corrected within 90 days (Sec. 34-527(d)).

cities.fines: Class C misdemeanor $200–$2,000 per violation per day; civil penalty up to $5,000 per violation per day. Unremedied notice of violation can lead to water/sewer shutoff (Sec. 34-531). Confirm current practice with SAWS.

cities.name: Miami-Dade County, FL
cities.agency: Miami-Dade Water and Sewer — FOG Control (Code §24-42.6)

pumping.accumulationRule: FOG capacity limit is 25% of design hydraulic depth (combined FOG + solids). Gravity interceptors are generally cleaned every 60 days or sooner to stay under 25%. Manual interceptors are typically monthly. Alternative frequencies may be approved, not to exceed 90 days.
pumping.waiver: Engineering analysis / field study can support an alternative frequency, capped at 90 days.
pumping.hauler: Use a permitted hauler unless a small interceptor qualifies for a self-cleaning exception. Keep logs.
pumping.permit: Annual FOG Discharge Control operating permit for qualifying FSEs.

cities.fines: Confirm current penalties with Miami-Dade WASD / permitting.

cities.name: Seattle, WA
cities.agency: Seattle Public Utilities — FOG / Commercial Kitchens

sources.label: Seattle Public Utilities FOG: commercial kitchens

pumping.accumulationRule: No fixed calendar interval on the SPU commercial-kitchens page. Clean per manufacturer specifications; if specs are not available, no more than 25 percent of an interceptor should contain food or FOG buildup. SMC 21.16.310 B (as quoted by SPU): clean when more than 25 percent full of grease and food waste. Each business sets a schedule from buildup rate. Emulsifying agents, enzymes, bio-additives, or similar chemicals are prohibited (SMC 21.16.310 D).
pumping.hauler: Many businesses use service providers; SPU publishes a FOG service-provider list. The same SPU page also describes self-cleaning indoor units (scoop solids, add absorbent, bag to dumpster). Use a maintenance log (SPU PDF).
pumping.permit: Any business with commercial kitchen plumbing fixtures and a King County Food Business Permit must install a grease interceptor (SPU; SMC 21.16.310 A). Even small delis, coffee shops, pizza parlors, and caterers.

cities.fines: SPU states fees range from $250 to $5,000 for non-compliance. The owner may also have to pay city costs from grease-laden wastewater damage. Confirm current amounts with SPU (greasefreepipes@Seattle.gov).
